fatal_errors: It replaces the tested as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA with an unspecified, surface-engineered HEA, potentially containing Ti.
It treats 600–1000 °C as the tribo-corrosion service range, whereas the target tests were aqueous at 25–100 °C; approximately 1100 °C was only transient thermal-shock conditioning.
It invents thermal oxidation or laser processing and a continuous self-healing spinel layer, none of which was the studied intervention or established mediator.
The cited evidence does not demonstrate that an engineered spinel layer improves HEA tribo-corrosion or survives repeated sliding.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad goal of improving HEA resistance to combined wear and corrosion and proposes a reasonably falsifiable treated-versus-untreated experiment. However, it does not reconstruct the studied material, intervention, environment, comparator, or temperature-dependent result. The target advantage arose from the stable L12/B2 lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 microstructure, robust aqueous passivation, and tribo-layer behavior relative to identically conditioned DS2205, with minimum degradation near 50 °C. The generated mechanism instead centers on a deliberately produced high-temperature spinel coating. E1 only supports protective oxides in general and also notes environmental instability; E2 and E3 do not substantiate the claimed surface-treatment, self-healing, or tribological mechanism. Thus the proposal is conceivable as a separate research direction but is not adequately supported by the supplied evidence.
